data.name: Body.MainExplanation.Lead
data.value: 아래에 있는 불필요한 파일은 모두 [안전하게 삭제할 수 있습니다].
data.comment: Main window intro, key 1 of 3 (the lead). Rendered prominent (heading tier): the reassurance the window opens on. "Any" and not "The": the same sentence shows over a count of zero, so it must read correctly with no files below it. Keep it one short clause. The bracketed phrase becomes a hyperlink into the README's "Is it safe?" section (rendered in MainWindow.xaml.cs BuildIntroLeadLine); the brackets are the delimiter and are not shown. This is the screen's strongest safety claim, so keep the brackets on whatever phrase carries that claim in this language.

data.name: Body.MainExplanation.Why
data.value: 이 파일들은 {InstallerFolder}에 있습니다. InstallerClean은 설치된 모든 프로그램에 대해 Windows에 문의합니다. 어떤 프로그램도 자기 것이라고 하지 않거나({0}), 더 새로운 패치가 그 파일을 대체했고 어떤 프로그램도 그 파일로 되돌아갈 수 없을 때({1}) 목록에 오릅니다.
data.comment: Main window intro, key 2 of 3 (the why, rendered muted). TWO PLACEHOLDERS, ONE PER CAUSE THE OFFER CAN CONTAIN: {0} is Reason.Orphaned and {1} is Reason.Superseded, the only two labels the scan sets (FileSystemScanService, the walked-file branch and the superseded-patch branch). Reason.Obsoleted is still passed as {2} by MainViewModel and is deliberately unused here: an obsoleted registration is counted at scan time and never offered, so naming that cause on this screen would describe a file the list cannot hold. Carrying the labels as placeholders means a translator edits each one in a single place and this sentence follows. THE OPENING CLAUSE CARRIES THE EPISTEMICS FOR BOTH HALVES: it says what the app asked, so what follows is read as the answer it got and not as an assertion about the machine. IT PARTITIONS BECAUSE THE SET HAS TWO CAUSES, and a sentence naming one of them is false of the other half: an orphan is offered because no registration claims its file, and a superseded patch is offered BECAUSE a registration does claim it and reports the patch replaced. THE SECOND CLAUSE'S ROLLBACK HALF IS NOT A RESTATEMENT OF ITS FIRST and must not be dropped as one in any language: replaced is not finished with, since uninstalling whatever replaced the patch can roll back onto it and reach for this exact file, which is the condition that decides whether a superseded patch is offered at all. The single-cause sentence this replaces was true only while the superseded class was withheld, which is a state no released version was ever in. BOTH CLAUSES ARE ABOUT THE ANSWER THE APP RECEIVED AND NOT ABOUT THE STATE OF THE MACHINE, which is the weaker claim and the one that stays true whatever an enumeration cannot see, so it is kept rather than tightened. The wording this replaces gave two reasons for that framing and neither survives at 3.0.0: the instance-code reading lost its subject once nothing read inside a cached file any more (see InstanceProductCount, which says so in its own words), and a recorded path spelled in a form the folder walk never produces is expanded and handled from 3.0.0 rather than guarded against (see NormaliseLocalPackagePath). The framing outlives its old reasons. Translations must keep both clauses statements about what came back; a rendering that says outright that Windows has no record of the file makes a claim about the machine that this wording exists to avoid.

data.name: Body.MainExplanation.Action
data.value: 직접 고른 백업 폴더로 옮긴 다음, 프로그램이 여전히 정상적으로 업데이트되고 제거되는지 확인되면 그 폴더를 삭제하세요. {InstallerFolder}에 다시 넣으면 모두 원래대로 돌아갑니다. 아니면 지금 영구히 삭제하세요.
data.comment: Main window intro, key 3 of 3 (the action, rendered in the body tier). MOVE IS NAMED FIRST AND DELETE LAST, REVERSING WHAT THIS LINE USED TO DO, and the reason is not doubt about the offer: the lead above says these files are safe to delete and that claim stands at full strength. It is that Move is the only route by which a person can satisfy themselves, and the app had never told anybody how, leaving a real user to work it out for himself and say so in public. THE MIDDLE CLAUSE IS THE WHOLE OF THAT INSTRUCTION AND BOTH OPERATIONS ARE NAMED ON PURPOSE: update and uninstall are what a cached package is kept for, so somebody who has done both and seen nothing break has exercised the thing the file exists for. Naming fewer leaves a person guessing what else to try. REPAIR IS DELIBERATELY NOT AMONG THEM, AND THE REASON IS WHAT A REPAIR ACTUALLY DOES. It does not read the cached package, so it can fail with the file present and succeed with it absent, which makes it silent about anything this app has done, and it fails for reasons that predate the app entirely. Somebody sent to try one, meeting a failure and concluding InstallerClean had broken their machine, is the worst thing this sentence could produce. "Then delete that folder" is the finish and must survive translation: without it the advice is to move files somewhere and keep them for ever, which reclaims nothing and is not what Move is for. THE THIRD SENTENCE STATES THE RESTORE PLAINLY AND CARRIES NO CONDITION, WHICH IS THE SAME DECISION AS THE ONE BELOW RATHER THAN A SEPARATE ONE: opening it with a condition, on the order of "if anything does go wrong", sits three lines under the lead's safe-to-delete claim and argues with it. WHAT MAKES THE PLAIN FORM HONEST IS IN THE MOVE ITSELF. A cached package counts as present if and only if its recorded LocalPackage path exists, so the name is the whole of what makes a restore work, and Move never renames: the file carries its own name into the backup folder, a name already taken there is refused rather than worked around, and every file on the offer sits directly in the cache folder, whichever half of the scan found it, because CandidateGuard.CheckSafeToRemove admits nothing else. Every file that moved therefore goes back to the exact path it came from, so the reader has nothing to get right and the line does not ask them to. Keep the folder named rather than "back where they were": it is the whole instruction, and it is the one thing the window never said before. NO QUALIFIER BELONGS ON THIS LINE, and a draft carrying one was rejected rather than never written. It would have sat three lines under the safe-to-delete claim and argued with it, and attaching it to Delete alone would imply Move protects against something the app declines to name, which is the shape a rival would have chosen. The screen's safety claim is ONE decision across the lead and this line and not two: anything that hedged here would have had to weaken the lead in the same pass. The limit is stated once, in the README, which the bracketed phrase in the lead links to. The button order is a separate matter and does not govern this line.

data.name: Body.RegisteredMissingFromDisk
data.value:
이 설치 파일이 없습니다. 지금은 아무 문제도 일으키지 않으며, 이 파일이 속한 프로그램을 업데이트하거나 제거하려는 날이 오기 전까지는 문제가 없습니다. 그때 Windows가 이 파일을 찾지 못해 그 단계가 실패할 수 있습니다.
되돌리려면 지금 사용 중인 버전의 설치 프로그램이 필요합니다. 프로그램 제작사에서 구해 기존 설치본 위에 실행하세요. 더 새 버전으로는 되지 않습니다. 새 버전은 먼저 지금 있는 것을 제거해야 하는데, 바로 그 단계에 이 파일이 필요하기 때문입니다. 먼저 제거하는 방법도 같은 이유로 되지 않습니다. 이렇게 하면 파일이 복원되고 설정은 그대로 남아야 하지만, Microsoft가 보장하지는 않습니다.
data.comment: Shown in the Registered Files details pane when a selected product's installer file is gone from disk. Generic with no product name interpolated: the recovery advice is identical for every program, and a possessive on a name ending in s reads wrongly.

data.value: Windows에 {InstallerFolder}에 없는 파일 {0}개의 기록이 있습니다: {1}. 평소에는 문제가 없지만 그 프로그램의 업데이트나 제거가 실패할 수 있습니다. 파일을 되돌리려면 지금 사용 중인 버전의 설치 프로그램이 필요합니다. 프로그램 제작사에서 구해 기존 설치본 위에 실행하세요. 더 새 버전으로는 되지 않습니다. 새 버전은 먼저 지금 있는 것을 제거해야 하는데, 바로 그 단계에 이 파일이 필요하기 때문입니다. 먼저 제거하는 방법도 같은 이유로 되지 않습니다. 이렇게 하면 파일이 복원되고 설정은 그대로 남아야 하지만, Microsoft가 보장하지는 않습니다.

data.value: # crash.log에는 InstallerClean의 처리되지 않은 예외가 기록됩니다. # 권한이 상승된 상태에서는 프레임워크의 예외 메시지에 실행 중인 # 세션의 파일 경로가 포함될 수 있습니다(Windows Installer 쿼리가 # 열거한 다른 사용자의 프로필 포함). 업데이트 확인이나 결과 로그 # 전송의 네트워크 실패 메시지에는 대상 URL과 확인된 IP 또는 프록시 # 주소가 포함될 수 있습니다. 읽을 수 없는 Windows Installer 기록에 # 대한 항목에는 Windows 계정 SID(S-1-5-21-...)와 설치된 소프트웨어의 # 제품 코드가 포함될 수 있습니다. # 이 파일을 공개 버그 신고에 첨부하기 전에 세 가지 정보를 모두 # 지우세요.
